A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Kernel Neural Operator work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions and some internal inconsistencies in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original KNO benchmark experiments, kernel and architecture ablations, sparsity measurements, and super-resolution results. Borrowed baseline results are separately identified.

after.justification: v2 reports original KNO and baseline experiments, including new forecasting and 3D tasks, component ablations, and training and inference measurements.

M1.justification: v1 primarily uses compact Wendland integration kernels followed by a spectral-mixture final layer. v2 instead uses GSM or neural nonstationary NS-GSM kernels throughout, adds dimension-wise factorization for regular grids, and revises irregular-domain data transfer to include interpolation after lifting and a return interpolant. These change the actual architecture and computation.

E1.justification: Burgers, Darcy PWC, and triangular Darcy remain. Advection, continuous-permeability Darcy, triangular-notch Darcy, and the 2D vorticity-prediction task disappear. v2 adds Beijing air-quality forecasting, geometry-to-velocity prediction in curved pipes, 3D compressible Navier–Stokes, and 3D reaction-diffusion on a point cloud, substantially changing the represented domains and task requirements.

E2.justification: v1 Table 1 compares against KM, DeepONet, POD-DeepONet, and FNO/dgFNO+. v2 Table 2 drops the first three families and adds GNOT. Within the retained triangular Darcy experiment, GeoFNO replaces dgFNO+; this is an actual comparator change, although GeoFNO was already discussed in v1.

E3.justification: Manual KNO tuning and dataset-specific training budgets become grid searches and a stated 10,000-epoch budget, except 500 epochs for NS-Pipe. Regular-grid integration switches to trapezoidal quadrature on the data grid. New timing experiments specify batches of 10 and averaging over 100 epochs. Sample-count changes cannot reliably be inferred from v2 Table 9, which contradicts the Burgers and Beijing-Air descriptions.

E4.justification: v1's NTK spectra, learned-sparsity analysis, and Burgers kernel-sharing studies are removed. v2 Appendix A.7 adds or substantially revises investigations of kernel expressivity, model size, integration versus pointwise convolution, quadrature resolution, and factorization's speed–accuracy tradeoff. The super-resolution example is retained rather than newly added.

E5.justification: v1 reports KNO means and standard deviations from nine runs: three train/test splits with three initializations each. v2 reports means and standard errors from four initializations, without documenting the earlier split-variation assessment. Its ablation tables report four-initialization means without the uncertainty bars shown in v1's ablation plots, substantially changing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores, parameter counts, ablation findings, and timing results are extensively replaced or added. For example, reported Burgers KNO/FNO percentage errors change from 0.52/1.93 in v1 Table 1 to 0.574/0.276 in v2 Table 2, reversing their within-version ranking under revised models and protocols. v2 also inconsistently reports Darcy PWC KNO error as 1.55 in Table 2 and 1.512 in Table 8.

T1.justification: v1 leaves universal approximation proofs to future work. v2 Section 3 and Appendix B introduce two stated approximation theorems, constructive Mercer-expansion and MLP lemmas, and a discretization bound involving fill distance, with explicit compactness, regularity, and quadrature assumptions. This adds substantial formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion shift the central contribution from compact-kernel sparsity to expressive neural kernels and flexible integration. v2 adds convergence and dimension-wise scalability claims, plus comparisons with GNOT. It also narrows the broad accuracy-superiority claim to comparable or higher accuracy and qualifies parameter savings as typical.

C2.justification: v1's explanations emphasizing Wendland smoothness, sparsity, and NTK spectra are replaced by discussions of kernel expressivity, difficult loss landscapes, interpolation placement, and quadrature effects. v2 adds interpretations of high-Mach failures and factorization tradeoffs, and distinguishes small parameter storage from runtime efficiency, attributing timing limitations partly to implementation.

D1.justification: v2 adds NS-GSM network width and mixture-size details, model-specific search ranges, learning-rate candidates, baseline repository references, and JAX/PyTorch and A100/A40 hardware information. Its appendices also document new datasets and quadrature choices. Conversely, v1's per-problem selected-configuration table and detailed freeze-training schedules are no longer supplied.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around transformer operators, neural nonstationary kernels, and approximation theory, citing GNOT, Transolver, Remes et al., and additional theoretical work. It also changes the stated FNO relationship: v1 contrasts KNO's diagonal kernels with dense FNO kernels, whereas v2 describes both as diagonal and emphasizes scalar-kernel flexibility instead.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodological explanation, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Results move from predominantly dataset-by-dataset exposition to cross-task accuracy, parameter-count, and timing sections. Architectural and benchmark descriptions are redistributed into reorganized appendices, and a theoretical section is inserted into the main narrative.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one-column to two-column layout, with substantially redesigned tables and separate main-text and appendix uncertainty displays. The architecture schematic, NTK plot, and several earlier experiment figures disappear; air-quality and 3D illustrations and numerous analysis tables are added. The quadrature illustration and super-resolution figure are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical credibility by replacing most borrowed baseline comparisons with tuned experiments under stated training budgets. Its 3D and real-data evaluations and component/timing studies directly address v1's untested applicability and scalability. These gains remain substantial despite reduced run/split coverage and reporting defects: Tables 2 and 8 disagree on Darcy PWC, Table 9 contradicts dataset descriptions, and Table 5 does not support the introduction's claim of faster 3D training than GNOT.
